alate: The vertex, pronotum and abdominal tergites are brownish, the mesonotum, metanotum, tibiae and abdominal sternites yellowish brown, the femora pale, the wing veins distinct. The body is rather large and robust, the ocelli rather large and elliptical, their distance from the compound eye less than the width of the ocellus. Antennae with 15 segments, the segments circular or oval. The anterior margin of the pronotum is almost straight and slightly raised at the middle, the two anterolateral corners slightly projecting forwards, the posterior margin narrower than the anterior, and an indistinct pale T-shaped mark in the middle of the disc. The forewing scale is slightly larger than the hindwing scale; the media of the forewing arises independently at the shoulder suture and lies close to the cubitus, beginning to branch beyond the midpoint of the wing length, with five or six branches in all reaching the wing apex, the cubitus with about eight branches; the media of the hindwing arises from the radial sector.
biology: It lives in the soil or inside dead tree roots, often together with capritermes-group termites and with Odontotermes; it has been found in the tunnels bored by Odontotermes in tree roots.
distribution: Shantou and Shaoguan, Guangdong; Pinghe, Fujian; Yunjinghong, Hekou, Pingbian, Jinping (Mengla), Mojiang, Santaishan, Simao and Manyun, Yunnan; abroad it is found in India.
soldier: The posterior part of the head is orange-yellow, gradually deepening forwards into orange-red; the mandibles black; the anterior part of the thorax and the abdomen white or tinged with pale yellow. The longitudinal suture of the head extends forwards from the posterior end for more than half the length of the head. The head is a rather large rectangle; the mandibles are robust, the apex of the left mandible curved outwards and blunt, the right mandible sabre-like. The anterior margin of the labrum is rather straight, the labrum longer than wide, the anterolateral corners projecting as short needles. Antennae with 14 segments, segments 1 to 3 longer than segment 4, segments 6 to 8 equal in length and all longer than segment 5, the segments gradually shortening from the ninth or tenth onwards, the apex of the terminal segment narrow and its length about equivalent to that of segment 5. The anterior and posterior margins of the pronotum have no notch, or occasionally an extremely indistinct one.
